items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled theorem wfetofe at source lines 980-983: weak function extensionality implies the full function extensionality axiom. The author's proof (source lines 985-1007) is a chain of reductions in which one link has to be weakened deliberately. Function extensionality is first reduced to the statement that the canonical map from identities of functions to homotopies induces an equivalence on total spaces (source lines 986-994); since the total space on the left is a type of pairs of a section with an identity, contractible by the characterisation of paths with one free endpoint, the goal becomes contractibility of the type of pairs of a section with a pointwise homotopy (source lines 995-999); transposing that type turns it into a product of contractible types, but the transposition result is proved using function extensionality for one of its two composites, so what survives is only a retraction, and the author records explicitly that a retract of a contractible type is contractible (source lines 1000-1006). The statement announces neither the retraction step nor the fact that the auxiliary transposition theorem has to be used one-sidedly.
